claims.text: Instrumented nanoindentation will reveal localized mechanical heterogeneities in FeNiCrMn HEA.
The localized mechanical heterogeneities revealed by nanoindentation are not captured by conventional global mechanical tests.
Varying strain rate and temperature during nanoindentation can help characterize localized mechanical behavior in FeNiCrMn HEA.
The initial FeNiCrMn HEA contains inherent microstructural heterogeneities.
Instrumented nanoindentation can locally measure hardness and elastic modulus.
In-situ SEM coupled with nanoindentation can observe deformation in real time.
Appropriate surface preparation can preserve microscale features needed for local mechanical characterization.
Grain boundaries and phase distributions influence local deformation behavior in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Nanoindentation provides sufficiently high spatial resolution to correlate local microstructure with local hardness and elastic modulus.
Correlations between local microstructure and indentation response can link microscale features to the alloy's overall mechanical behavior.
Localized nanoindentation measurements will show significant scatter in mechanical properties.
The scatter in local mechanical properties will correlate with microstructural heterogeneities.
Nanoindentation will provide deformation-mechanism insights that differ from those obtained through macroscopic mechanical tests.
Previous FeNiCrMn HEA studies have focused primarily on corrosion resistance and global mechanical tests.
Previous FeNiCrMn HEA studies lack high-resolution local mechanical-property measurements.
Spatial variability may be greatest in as-cast or minimally processed FeNiCrMn HEA.
Homogenizing post-processing may diminish the observed local mechanical variability.
High-strain-rate nanoindentation measurements may complicate interpretation.
The quantitative relationship between local nanoindentation observations and global mechanical performance is uncertain.
